summary: Recent midterm election results have energized statehood advocates, who point to D.C.'s population size as support for equal representation, while the District has faced multiple recent challenges to its local authority that courts and Congress are now contesting. Without statehood, D.C. residents have no senators, and their one delegate to the House cannot vote on the House floor.
